issue.title: Idle TUI accumulates NotificationPlusOne objects (16k-22k -> 28.5k live over 2 h)

task_type_fields.impact: Idle long-lived TUI sessions accumulate notification +1 objects at about 6k per hour, adding to the chronic heap and gen-2 GC work tracked in sase-1nc. The store payload and parse cost for heavily +1'd notification rows grow without bound.
task_type_fields.repro:
`sase.notifications.models.NotificationPlusOne` (built in `src/sase/core/notification_store_wire.py:279`) keeps growing in an idle TUI. The sase-1t3.9 post-storm GC census (note #5 on sase-1t3.9 and the ranked list in sase-1t3 note #4, item 7) recorded:

- 22,368 live (1.07 MB) at 10 min (instance d5ac2b89, `~/.sase/perf/sase-1t3.9/gc_census_20261117T111640Z`).
- 16,212 at about 65 min on a second soak (2e14b925).
- 28,547 live (1.37 MB) at 2 h idle (instance 39893a35, `gc_census_20261117T145641Z`), alongside 8,454 live `Notification` objects.

Notification +1s are append-only and the same sender may repeat (see the dataclass docstring), so a notification row that is +1'd on every recurrence keeps a list that grows without bound. Every notification snapshot the TUI keeps (inbox model, modal caches, wire conversions) retains the full history. The bead-touch, artifact-read, and memory-read lanes were bounded in sase-1t3.11; notifications were outside that phase's scope.

Investigate first. Identify which TUI owner keeps these objects alive (`SASE_TUI_GC_CENSUS=1` with the census watchlist, or `gc.get_referrers` on a sample) and which senders produce long +1 tails (`jq` over the notification store). Then bound retention: cap or compact stored +1 entries per row, or project only a count plus the latest N for list paint and hydrate the full list for the selected row only.

issue.creation_reason: Proposed by sase-1t3.9 note #5 (post-storm GC census); the growth was outside the sase-1t3 heap-diet phases' scope and no existing task tracks it.
